locator.text: Equation (5.13), p. 50, in the statement of Lemma 5.2

evidence: paper: |\partial^I \mathcal{T}_n(X,\eta)| \le C_{n,I}\,\zeta(X)\,\delta(X)^{-N_{n,I}} \qquad (X_a < X < X_b,\ |\eta|\le 1). \tag{5.13}  % followed by: "Here C_{n,I}, N_{n,I} may depend on the order and derivative; for n \ge 2 one may take N_{n,I}=0."  \delta(X)=\min\{1,\log(X/X_a),\log(X_b/X)\}, \zeta the flat weight of Theorem 4.6(iv), \mathcal{T}_n=(\mathcal{T}_{n,\theta},\mathcal{T}_{n,z}) from (5.9).

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The inequality is the body of PolynomialEdgeJets with the paper's ingredients: activeDelta a b w = min 1 (min (log X - a) (b - log X)) is δ(X) with a = log X_a, b = log X_b; activeWindow a b = Ioo (exp a) (exp b) × Icc (-1) 1 is the paper's range; activeZeta is a two-edge flat weight in log X; stressPair d n = (stressTheta n, stressAxial n) are the two components of (5.9). The Lean bounds the whole order-m derivative tensor with C, N existential per order m, which is the paper's "C_{n,I}, N_{n,I} may depend on the order and derivative" up to the finite-dimensional norm. No single declaration states the bound for all n ≥ 1; it is split as the paper itself splits it. n = 1: modulated_first_edgeJets states it on the outer collar for the constructed coefficients, and edgeJets_of_outer_collar (with the zero germ from modulated_positive_stress_zero) extends it to the whole window; that combination is carried out inside modulated_weighted_on_actual_scales rather than recorded as a separate theorem. n ≥ 2: no theorem concludes PolynomialEdgeJets for stressPair d n, but SlowStressSupport.interior_weighted_jets is stated for an arbitrary continuous positive weight on Ioo l r, and instantiating it with zeta := radialWeight c left right, S := univ, K := Icc (-1) 1, f := stressTheta n / stressAxial n, with support hypotheses from modulated_higherInteriorSupport and smoothness from modulated_smooth, gives |∂^k T_n| ≤ C ζ(X) on the window, i.e. (5.13) with N = 0, exactly the paper's closing remark. I did not find that instantiation written out anywhere; the repository instead consumes the n ≥ 2 case as smoothness of T_n/ζ (modulated_quotients_smooth). Finding B's route for n ≥ 2 through logarithmic_weighted_jets is not the right one (its weight logFlatWeight is in log R and needs an unrecorded rescaling of the edge constants); the generic interior_weighted_jets needs no such step. Not verified: that activeZeta c a b (left constant c > 0 arbitrary, right constant 4) is literally the weight ζ of Theorem 4.6(iv); I matched only its two-edge flat form.
